statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains at the watch floor on observed two-sided overnight structure, while high cross-asset Stress persists from a 24-year-high Treasury curve and a ~4.4% Brent jump ahead of the 12:30Z September payrolls release.
recommendation: Tail stays below the block threshold for the current hour. A narrow evidence-based danger window is published for 12:30Z-14:00Z, covering the September payrolls print and the U.S. cash open, where the forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: NQ holds a narrow overnight band near 30,861 as a 24-year-high yield curve and a Brent spike meet the September payrolls print
body:
Observed at the assessment cutoff: NQ futures trade 30,861.25, up 0.33%, inside a narrow ~110-point overnight band between 30,760.25 and 30,869.75. Cash NDX closed Thursday at 30,501.56, up 0.31%, after recovering from a 30,274.65 session low within a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range, and VIX decayed from a 17.59 intraday high to 16.39. That combination is observed mean reversion working, not failing, which is why Tail sits at the watch floor.

The Stress picture is materially worse than the price action. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34% on Thursday, a 24-year high and the highest since 2002, before easing toward 5.24%; H.15 records 5.29% for September 30 with the 2-year at 4.88%, after the bond market's worst quarter in decades. Brent jumped roughly 4.4% to $102.42 on Strait of Hormuz and US-Iran disruption risk, with Murban up 6.99% showing a concentrated Gulf-shipping premium, and WTI near $93. Semiconductors are the offsetting support after Micron reported $33.42 EPS on $54.23 billion revenue and guided first-quarter revenue to about $61.5 billion at an 87% gross margin.

These cross-asset signals conflict with firm equities, so they raise Stress and not Tail. The single dated catalyst is the September employment report at 12:30Z, consensus 90,000 after August's 162,000, with the unemployment rate seen unchanged at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.2% month over month; reporting ahead of the release flagged scope for an upside surprise following the ADP print and the fewest September job cuts since 2022. Initial claims for the week ended September 26 came in at 197,000 against a 200,000 expectation. The specific mechanism the published danger window guards is a hot print repricing a curve that is already at a 24-year high, which is the one credible route to a delayed second leg; event importance and surprise magnitude alone do not establish a pathological price path, so the forecast peaks at Tail 25 for only the two hours spanning the print and the cash open.

Evidence completeness caveat: the shared Finviz context file was collected 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial and unavailable futures and calendar sections, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used. The economic-calendar aggregator consulted also returned column-misaligned values, so release timing was verified directly against the BLS and Federal Reserve schedules instead. September CPI is scheduled for October 14 and therefore falls outside the seven-day window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held the 20-24 watch band throughout October 1 with a single 25 print at 06:00Z, while Stress rose from 70 to a 78 peak around the 14:00Z-15:00Z window and Confidence held at 87-89. The pattern is a persistently stressed but mean-reverting environment rather than a developing one-way path.
outlookSummary: The base case keeps Tail in the 20-23 watch band through the Asian and European sessions on observed two-sided structure, then raises it to 25 for the two hours spanning the 12:30Z September payrolls release and the 13:30Z U.S. cash open, where the forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail eases from 14:00Z on the base case that price discovery turns orderly and retracements resume, with a modest 22 tick into the Friday power hour for late continuation and weekend-headline positioning. Stress stays high throughout, peaking near 82 in the release window, because a 24-year-high Treasury curve and a Brent spike persist independently of the equity path.
